items.title: Gilead snags equity stake in Vir with up to $1.87B deal for three T cell engagers
items.snippet: The Gilead Sciences deal, which include $135 million in upfront and near-term payments, marks a critical platform validation for Vir Biotechnology as investors await an upcoming readout in solid tumors.

items.title: Verastem reports ‘robust’ response rate in pancreatic cancer subgroup where Rasonque struggled
items.snippet: Revolution Medicines’ recently approved drug showed a 24% overall response rate and a high rate of side effects in patients whose cancer has a G12D mutation, reinforcing Mizuho’s view that a more specific agent such as Verastem Oncology’s VS-7375 “should come first for G12D patients.”

items.title: ‘Pharma bro’ Shkreli runs afoul of court’s lifetime pharma ban
items.snippet: Since his release from prison in 2022, Martin Shkreli has traded stocks and publicly opined on news events, damaging reputations and sinking share prices for small biotechs including Capricor and Cassava, the FTC alleges.

items.title: GSK plans 1.2K+ layoffs at Belgium sites as $2.5B restructure gains momentum
items.snippet: The layoffs across GSK’s Belgium sites come on the heels of the pharma’s planned shuttering of its German vaccine manufacturing site, which prompted job cuts for about 650 employees.

items.title: Zealand pens up to $1.2B deal with Generate for AI-designed obesity, metabolic drugs
items.snippet: Obesity-focused Zealand Pharma is buying into Generate:Biomedicines’s generative AI platform to create new multispecific drug candidates.

items.title: Verdiva ends mid-stage study of oral GLP-1 amid ‘market evolution’
items.snippet: The candidate is an oral version of ecnoglutide, a subcutaneous formulation of which is approved in China for type 2 diabetes and weight management. Pfizer owns commercialization rights for ecnoglutide in the Asian country.

items.title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
items.snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

items.title: Alnylam bulls and bears fight it out after business-shaking guidance cut
items.snippet: While Alnylam’s recent reduced revenue guidance spooked investors, analysts remain broadly bullish on the biotech’s commercial prospects.

items.title: J&J’s disappointing Q3, RevMed’s subgroup data, BMS’ ‘mixed’ results, Caribou’s cutback
items.snippet: Johnson & Johnson beat analyst expectations in the third quarter but left Wall Street wanting more; BMS dominated the news cycle on Monday with a Phase 3 win validating its $4.1 billion RayzeBio buy and mixed data in a late-stage pulmonary fibrosis trial; Revolution Medicines’ newly approved pancreatic cancer drug wor...

items.title: European biotech leaders split on US-China fight for deal dominance, survey finds
items.snippet: While industry leaders are unsure whether the U.S. or China will prevail, they are largely united in the belief that Europe is lagging behind.

items.title: Jazz CEO calls on industry to help rebuild momentum for leadership diversity
items.snippet: The first-time CEO says her own sponsors took chances on her—and that industry leaders need to do the same to rebuild momentum for gender equity.

items.title: J&J’s innovative medicines carried Q3 as medtech disappoints, but newer medicines absent
items.snippet: While innovative medicine supported Johnson & Johnson’s “in line” earnings for the third quarter of 2026, investors were disappointed to see older medicines carrying the bag.

items.title: BioNTech faces 3rd mRNA setback as head and neck cancer therapy fails to improve survival
items.snippet: While BNT113 failed to improve progression-free survival in patients with a type of head and neck cancer during a Phase 3 trial, BioNTech is holding out hope for an overall survival win—but analysts say that outcome is now "less likely."

items.title: Roche expands obesity R&D footprint with Rona deal worth $1B+
items.snippet: Roche has gained access to a genetic obesity approach from China's Rona Therapeutics for up to $100 million in upfront and near-term payments.

items.title: Syndax ends fibrosis program for Niktimvo after mid-stage disappointment
items.snippet: Syndax Pharmaceuticals will no longer test Niktimvo for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, but the company’s work to expand the drug’s label in chronic graft-versus-host disease, for which it was approved in 2024, will continue.

items.title: Pfizer pens $500M+ deal with Enodia to destroy disease-causing proteins
items.snippet: After Pfizer’s venture arm co-led Enodia Therapeutics’ $25 million seed round in January, the pharma has signed up to collaborate with the biotech on small-molecule drugs to eliminate pathogenic proteins where they’re being made.

items.title: Analysts eye RevMed’s pancreatic cancer launch, Merck’s data blitz for Q3 earnings
items.snippet: Bellwether Johnson & Johnson will kick off the third quarter earnings reporting period on Tuesday, with analysts searching for news on business development, launch execution and more.

items.title: BMS’ Phase 3 win for lung drug clouded by high-dose miss
items.snippet: A low-dose win could derisk a regulatory pathway for BMS’ LPA1 antagonist in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis after a recently reported patient death, but a miss at the higher dose leaves analysts awaiting full data.

items.title: RevMed's Rasonque gets a subtype data asterisk, but analysts remain bullish
items.snippet: Data released by the FDA show that Revolution Medicine’s newly approved pancreatic cancer drug underperformed in a large subgroup of patients, but analysts say the biotech still has a clear winner.

items.title: BMS’ $4.1B RayzeBio bet delivers Phase 3 radiopharma win
items.snippet: The centerpiece of Bristol Myers Squibb’s 2024 RayzeBio buy has read out, hitting the primary endpoint in a late-stage tumor trial.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
